S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms that develop in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor and become clinically significant through disproportionate distress or functional impairment. It typically begins within a short period after the stressor, often improves when the stressor or its consequences resolve, and does not meet criteria for another primary mental disorder. It is distinguished from ordinary stress by the degree of disruption it causes in daily functioning and from conditions such as PTSD or major depressive disorder by its stress-linked, subthreshold, and usually time-limited course.

patient.stressor: Jeffrey’s wife’s parents began staying with them for an open-ended period after a family dispute over finances and caregiving, and the arrangement quickly disrupted the orderly home environment he relied on to manage demanding client negotiations. What began as irritation over schedules, privacy, and unsolicited criticism of his work hours intensified over the next month into a stress response that affected both his marriage and his performance at the agency. He postponed key decisions on a musician’s contract, became unavailable during a community theatre planning deadline, and had repeated conflicts at home that made the family situation clinically significant rather than merely inconvenient. After a near-missed deal prompted his managing partner to question his reliability and his wife insisted they needed outside help, Jeffrey arranged an appointment with a psychiatrist affiliated with his primary care network.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I’m here because since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve been so keyed up and worn down that I’m snapping at my wife, avoiding calls I would normally handle immediately, and I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.

add_requirements.Symptoms must develop within 3 months of: I was functioning normally before my in-laws moved in, and this all started within a few weeks of them taking over the house.
add_requirements.Within 6 months of the termination of th: The living arrangement still hasn’t ended, so these problems are happening while the in-law situation is still active, not months after it was resolved.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At work, I nearly lost a musician’s contract and my managing partner questioned whether I could still be trusted with major negotiations. At home, the conflict has gotten serious enough that my wife pushed for outside help.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a month, since my in-laws moved into our home.
